tools.name: get_connection_info
tools.title: Get connection info
tools.description: Returns the name and address of the connected learning site, the name of the signed-in user, the profile and access level chosen for this connection, its scopes and its usage limits. Use it to find out which site and account the connection belongs to and whether it allows changes. It reads no course data.

tools.name: list_my_courses
tools.title: List my courses
tools.description: Returns the courses the signed-in user is enrolled in, with the user's roles in each course, start and end dates, completion progress and a link to the course. Use it to find a course by name and to get the course identifier that other tools take. Courses the site has excluded from the connector are not listed. Returns at most 50 courses per call; use 'cursor' to continue.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return.

cursor.description: Value of 'next_cursor' from a previous call, to continue from there.

tools.name: search_courses
tools.title: Search courses
tools.description: Returns the courses visible to the signed-in user whose name or summary matches a text, with their category and a link. Use it to find a course the user is not enrolled in or whose exact name is not known. Courses the site has excluded from the connector are not listed. Fields whose name ends in '_user_content' hold text written by course teachers and are returned as written. Considers at most 200 matches and returns at most 50 per call; use 'cursor' to continue.

search_text.description: Text to look for in course names and summaries.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return.

cursor.description: Value of 'next_cursor' from a previous call, to continue from there.

tools.name: get_course_outline
tools.title: Get course outline
tools.description: Returns the sections of one course and, for each section, the activities and resources the signed-in user can see, with their type, dates and a link. Use it to see how a course is organised or to find an activity. File contents are not returned. Fields whose name ends in '_user_content' hold text written by course participants or teachers and are returned as written. Returns at most 50 sections per call; use 'cursor' to continue.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return.

cursor.description: Value of 'next_cursor' from a previous call, to continue from there.

tools.name: list_upcoming_deadlines
tools.title: List upcoming deadlines
tools.description: Returns the signed-in user's upcoming course deadlines (assignments, quizzes and other activities with a due date) within a date range, ordered by date. Use it to answer questions about what is due and when. Returns at most 50 items per call; use 'cursor' to continue.

days_ahead.description: Number of days from today to include.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return.

cursor.description: Value of 'next_cursor' from a previous call, to continue from there.

tools.name: get_assignment_details
tools.title: Get assignment details
tools.description: Returns the description and dates of one assignment and the state of the signed-in user's own submission to it. Use it to answer what an assignment asks for, when it is due and whether the user has already submitted. 'assignment_id' is the activity identifier returned by get_course_outline. Submissions of other users and file contents are not returned. Fields whose name ends in '_user_content' hold text written by course teachers and are returned as written.

assignment_id.description: Activity identifier of the assignment, as returned by get_course_outline.

tools.name: list_course_announcements
tools.title: List course announcements
tools.description: Returns the most recent announcements of one course, newest first, with their subject, text, author name and date. Use it to see what the teachers have announced. Only the announcements forum of the course is read; other forums are not. Fields whose name ends in '_user_content' hold text written by course teachers and are returned as written. Returns at most 50 announcements per call; use 'cursor' to continue.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return.

cursor.description: Value of 'next_cursor' from a previous call, to continue from there.

tools.name: get_my_grades
tools.title: Get my grades
tools.description: Returns the signed-in user's own grades. Without 'course_id' it returns the overall grade in each course; with 'course_id' it returns every grade item of that course with the grade, the range and the teacher's feedback. Grades the site hides from the user are not revealed. Fields whose name ends in '_user_content' hold text written by teachers and are returned as written. Returns at most 50 items per call; use 'cursor' to continue.

course_id.description: Return the grade items of this course.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return.

cursor.description: Value of 'next_cursor' from a previous call, to continue from there.

tools.name: get_my_course_progress
tools.title: Get my course progress
tools.description: Returns the signed-in user's own completion of one course: whether the course is complete, the progress percentage and, for each activity with completion tracking that the user can see, whether it is complete. Use it to answer what the user still has to do in a course. Completion of other users is not returned. Returns at most 50 activities per call; use 'cursor' to continue.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return.

cursor.description: Value of 'next_cursor' from a previous call, to continue from there.

tools.name: list_course_participants
tools.title: List course participants
tools.description: Returns the participants of one course that the signed-in user teaches, with their roles, groups and, when the site shows it to this user, their last access to the course and e-mail address. Use it to see who is in a course or to get the user identifiers that other tools take. In a course with separate groups only members of the user's own groups are listed. Returns at most 50 participants per call; use 'cursor' to continue.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return.

cursor.description: Value of 'next_cursor' from a previous call, to continue from there.

tools.name: list_submissions_to_grade
tools.title: List submissions to grade
tools.description: Returns the assignment submissions waiting for a grade in one course the signed-in user teaches, or in one assignment of it, with the date submitted and the days waiting. Use it to see what is pending to grade; pass 'submission_id' to get_submission to read one. While an assignment uses anonymous marking, students appear as numbered participants. In a course with separate groups only submissions from the user's own groups are listed. Returns at most 50 submissions per call; use 'cursor' to continue, and 'scan_incomplete' is true when a very large course was only partly examined.

assignment_id.description: Limit results to one assignment: its activity identifier from get_course_outline.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return.

cursor.description: Value of 'next_cursor' from a previous call, to continue from there.

tools.name: get_submission
tools.title: Get submission
tools.description: Returns one assignment submission that the signed-in user may grade: its status and date, the text typed online, the name, size and type of each attached file, and the current grade if there is one. Use it to read a submission found with list_submissions_to_grade. File contents and download links are not returned. While the assignment uses anonymous marking, the student appears as a numbered participant. Fields whose name ends in '_user_content' hold text written by the student and are returned as written.

submission_id.description: Identifier of the submission, as returned by list_submissions_to_grade.

tools.name: get_course_grade_summary
tools.title: Get course grade summary
tools.description: Returns the gradebook of one course the signed-in user teaches: the grade items and, for each graded participant, the grade in each item and the course total. Use it to review how a group is doing or to find who has not been graded. In a course with separate groups only members of the user's own groups are listed. At most 60 grade items are included. Returns at most 50 participants per call; use 'cursor' to continue.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return.

cursor.description: Value of 'next_cursor' from a previous call, to continue from there.

tools.name: get_course_completion_report
tools.title: Get course completion report
tools.description: Returns, for one course the signed-in user teaches, whether each tracked participant has completed the course, the date of completion and the progress percentage. Use it to see who has finished and who is behind. If completion tracking is off in the course the list is empty. In a course with separate groups only members of the user's own groups are listed. Returns at most 50 participants per call; use 'cursor' to continue.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return.

cursor.description: Value of 'next_cursor' from a previous call, to continue from there.

tools.name: list_inactive_participants
tools.title: List inactive participants
tools.description: Returns the participants of one course the signed-in user teaches who have not accessed the course for a given number of days, or have never accessed it, with their last access. Use it to find who may need a reminder. It is refused when the site hides last access from this user. In a course with separate groups only members of the user's own groups are listed. Returns at most 50 participants per call; use 'cursor' to continue.

days.description: Number of days without access to the course.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return.

cursor.description: Value of 'next_cursor' from a previous call, to continue from there.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.title: List course categories
tools.description: Returns the course categories the signed-in user manages, with their full path, parent and number of courses. Use it to find the category identifier that other tools take. Categories the site has excluded from the connector and categories the user does not manage are not listed. Returns at most 50 categories per call; use 'cursor' to continue.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return.

cursor.description: Value of 'next_cursor' from a previous call, to continue from there.

tools.name: get_course_enrolment_summary
tools.title: Get course enrolment summary
tools.description: Returns, for one course the signed-in user manages, the enrolment methods with their state and number of enrolled users, the total of enrolled users and the number of users in each role. Use it to check how people get into a course and how many there are. Enrolment keys and other settings of the methods are not returned, and no individual user is listed.

tools.name: find_users
tools.title: Find users
tools.description: Returns up to 20 user accounts of the site whose name matches a text of at least 3 characters, with their identifier and a link. Use it to get the user identifiers that other tools take, for example before enrolling named people. The e-mail address is searched and returned only when the site shows e-mail addresses to this user. Deleted accounts are never returned, and there is no way to list all users: a search with more than 20 matches returns the first 20 and says so.

search_text.description: Part of the name, or of the e-mail address when the site shows it to this user.

tools.name: get_site_status
tools.title: Get site status
tools.description: Returns a short health summary of the site for its administrator: the major version, whether maintenance mode is on, when cron last ran and whether it is overdue, how many scheduled and background tasks are failing, and the number of user accounts and courses. Use it for a quick check of the site. Configuration values, server paths, the exact build and secrets are not returned.

tools.name: list_scheduled_tasks
tools.title: List scheduled tasks
tools.description: Returns the scheduled tasks of the site for its administrator, with the component each belongs to, when it last ran, when it runs next, whether it is disabled and whether it is failing. Use it to find tasks that do not run or keep failing. Set 'only_failing' to list just those. Task output and logs are not returned. Returns at most 50 tasks per call; use 'cursor' to continue.

only_failing.description: List only tasks whose last run failed.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return.

cursor.description: Value of 'next_cursor' from a previous call, to continue from there.

tools.name: list_installed_plugins
tools.title: List installed plugins
tools.description: Returns the plugins installed on the site for its administrator, with their component name, display name, release, whether they are enabled and their installation state. Use it to check what is installed or to find plugins that need attention. By default only additional plugins are listed; set 'include_standard' to list the ones that come with the site software too. Plugin settings are not returned. Returns at most 50 plugins per call; use 'cursor' to continue.

include_standard.description: Also list the plugins that are part of the standard distribution.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return.

cursor.description: Value of 'next_cursor' from a previous call, to continue from there.

tools.name: get_pending_action_status
tools.title: Get pending action status
tools.description: Returns the state of one change requested earlier through this connection that needs the user's approval on the site: pending, executed, rejected, expired or failed, with the summary of the change and the page where the user approves or rejects it. Use it after a tool answered 'approval_pending' to learn the outcome. It does not approve or change anything. Only actions created by this same connection can be read.

action_id.description: Identifier of the pending action, as returned by the tool that requested it.

tools.name: get_course_activity_log
tools.title: Get course activity log
tools.description: Returns the events of the standard log of one course the signed-in user teaches in a period of at most 31 days, newest first: when, who, the event, the activity and where it came from, optionally for one participant or one activity. Use it to see what happened in a course or what one learner did. Anonymous events, network addresses and the internal data of events are never returned, and in a course with separate groups only members of the user's own groups appear. Returns at most 50 events per call; use 'cursor' to continue.

from.description: Start of the period, ISO 8601 with a time zone, for example 2027-03-01T00:00:00+01:00.

to.description: End of the period, ISO 8601 with a time zone. At most 31 days after the start.

activity_id.description: Only events of this activity (course module identifier from get_course_outline).

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return.

cursor.description: Value of 'next_cursor' from a previous call, to continue from there.

tools.name: get_activity_participation_report
tools.title: Get activity participation report
tools.description: Returns, for one activity of a course the signed-in user teaches and a period of at most 31 days, each learner with the number of times they viewed it and the number of times they posted or submitted in it, including those who did neither. Use it to see who has not opened an activity yet. Counts come from the standard log, without anonymous events, and in a course with separate groups only members of the user's own groups are listed. Returns at most 50 learners per call; use 'cursor' to continue.

activity_id.description: Course module identifier of the activity, from get_course_outline.

from.description: Start of the period, ISO 8601 with a time zone, for example 2027-03-01T00:00:00+01:00.

to.description: End of the period, ISO 8601 with a time zone. At most 31 days after the start.

only_without_activity.description: List only learners who neither viewed nor posted in the period.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return.

cursor.description: Value of 'next_cursor' from a previous call, to continue from there.

tools.name: get_activity_completion_report
tools.title: Get activity completion report
tools.description: Returns, for one course the signed-in user teaches, the activities that track completion and, for each tracked participant, which of them they have completed, passed or failed and how many are still pending. Use it to see who is behind on which activity. Activities hidden from the user are left out, and in a course with separate groups only members of the user's own groups are listed. Returns at most 50 participants per call; use 'cursor' to continue.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return.

cursor.description: Value of 'next_cursor' from a previous call, to continue from there.

tools.name: get_quiz_attempts_report
tools.title: Get quiz attempts report
tools.description: Returns, for one quiz of a course the signed-in user teaches, each learner who may attempt it with the number of attempts, the state of the last one and the highest grade, including those who have not started. Use it to see who has done a quiz and how they scored. Questions and answers are never returned, teacher previews are left out, and with separate groups only members of the user's own groups are listed. Returns at most 50 learners per call; use 'cursor' to continue.

quiz_id.description: Course module identifier of the quiz, from get_course_outline.

only_without_attempts.description: List only learners who have not finished any attempt.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return.

cursor.description: Value of 'next_cursor' from a previous call, to continue from there.

tools.name: get_course_progress_summary
tools.title: Get course progress summary
tools.description: Returns figures about the learners of one course the signed-in user teaches, without naming anyone: how many there are, average and median progress percentage, how many are in each range of progress, how many completed the course, never entered it, have not entered for a number of days, and have overdue assignments. Use it to answer how a course or a group is doing; the names come from the completion, inactivity and overdue tools. With separate groups only the user's own groups are counted.

group_id.description: Count only the members of this group of the course.

inactive_days.description: Days without entering the course after which a learner counts as inactive.

tools.name: list_overdue_submissions
tools.title: List overdue submissions
tools.description: Returns the learners of one course the signed-in user grades who have assignments past their due date and not submitted, each with those assignments, the due date that applies to them (overrides and extensions included) and the days overdue. Use it to see who is behind and on what. Team assignments and assignments with blind marking are left out and counted, and with separate groups only members of the user's own groups are listed. Returns at most 50 learners per call; use 'cursor' to continue.

assignment_id.description: Only this assignment (course module identifier from get_course_outline).

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return.

cursor.description: Value of 'next_cursor' from a previous call, to continue from there.

tools.name: list_course_forums
tools.title: List course forums
tools.description: Returns the forums of one course the signed-in user teaches that they can read: name, type, number of discussions, date of the last post and whether the user may start a discussion there. Use it to find the forum to read or post in; the forum identifier is the one the other forum tools take.

tools.name: list_forum_discussions
tools.title: List forum discussions
tools.description: Returns the discussions of one forum of a course the signed-in user teaches, most recent activity first: subject, who started it, number of replies, last activity and whether it is pinned or locked. Use it to find a discussion to read or answer. The forum applies its own rules on groups and timed discussions. Returns at most 50 discussions per call; use 'cursor' to continue.

forum_id.description: Course module identifier of the forum, from list_course_forums.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return.

cursor.description: Value of 'next_cursor' from a previous call, to continue from there.

tools.name: get_forum_discussion
tools.title: Get forum discussion
tools.description: Returns the posts of one forum discussion that the signed-in user can read, oldest first: author, date, subject, the post it answers and the text as plain text, without attachments. Use it to read a discussion before answering it; the post identifiers are the ones reply_to_forum_post takes. Hidden text is removed. Returns at most 50 posts per call; use 'cursor' to continue.

discussion_id.description: Identifier of the discussion, from list_forum_discussions.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return.

cursor.description: Value of 'next_cursor' from a previous call, to continue from there.

tools.name: get_forum_participation_summary
tools.title: Get forum participation summary
tools.description: Returns, for one forum of a course the signed-in user teaches, each learner with the number of discussions they started, the number of replies they posted and the date of their last post, including those who have not posted, optionally within a period. Use it to see who takes part in a forum. Only posts the user could see on the forum pages are counted, and with separate groups only members of the user's own groups are listed. Returns at most 50 learners per call; use 'cursor' to continue.

forum_id.description: Course module identifier of the forum, from list_course_forums.

from.description: Count only posts from this moment, ISO 8601 with a time zone.

to.description: Count only posts before this moment, ISO 8601 with a time zone.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return.

cursor.description: Value of 'next_cursor' from a previous call, to continue from there.

tools.name: get_site_activity_summary
tools.title: Get site activity summary
tools.description: Returns, for the site administrator and a period of at most 31 days, how many distinct users signed in and how many sign-ins there were, failed sign-ins, course views, distinct active users, the same figures day by day in the user's time zone, and the ten most viewed courses. Use it to answer how many visits or accesses the site had today or this week. Only counts are returned, never who; anonymous events and the guest account are left out.

from.description: Start of the period, ISO 8601 with a time zone, for example 2027-03-01T00:00:00+01:00.

to.description: End of the period, ISO 8601 with a time zone. At most 31 days after the start.

tools.name: list_failed_tasks
tools.title: List failed tasks
tools.description: Returns, for the site administrator, the scheduled tasks that are failing, the ad hoc tasks waiting after a failure and the latest failed runs in the task log, each run with an excerpt of its output of at most 2000 characters. Use it to find out why background processing fails. Server paths, network addresses and e-mail addresses are replaced in the excerpt, and an excerpt that looks like it holds a password, key or token is withheld whole. Task data is never returned.

tools.name: get_site_checks
tools.title: Get site checks
tools.description: Returns, for the site administrator, the result of the status, security or performance checks of the site: each check with its name, component, state (ok, info, warning, error, critical, unknown or not applicable) and a plain text summary. Use it to see what needs attention on the site. The checks run when called; one that fails is reported as unknown, and those left when the time budget runs out are reported as not run.

only_problems.description: Return only checks whose state is warning, error, critical or unknown.

tools.name: save_assignment_grade
tools.title: Save assignment grade
tools.description: Saves a grade and optional feedback comment for one student's submission to one assignment, replacing any existing grade unless it is locked or overridden, and never changing its marking workflow state, so an unreleased grade stays hidden from the student. The student is named with 'user_id', or with 'submission_id' when marking is anonymous. Called without 'confirm_token', it changes nothing and returns a summary of the change plus a token valid for 5 minutes; called again with the same arguments and that token, it applies the change. Where approval is required it returns 'approval_pending' with a link to a page on the site where the signed-in user approves or rejects the change. Repeating a confirmed call returns the stored result and does not apply the change twice.

assignment_id.description: Identifier of the assignment activity, as returned by 'get_course_outline'.

user_id.description: Student to grade. Give this or 'submission_id', not both.

submission_id.description: Submission to grade, as returned by 'list_submissions_to_grade'.

grade.description: Grade on the assignment's own scale: points up to its maximum, or the position of the item when the assignment uses a scale.

feedback.description: Feedback comment for the student, as plain text.

notify_student.description: Whether the site notifies the student of the new grade.

confirm_token.description: Token returned by the first call, sent back with the same arguments to apply the change.

idempotency_key.description: Optional key chosen by the caller. Repeating a call with the same key and arguments returns the stored result instead of requesting the change again.

tools.name: post_course_announcement
tools.title: Post course announcement
tools.description: Publishes one announcement, with a subject and a plain text message, in the announcements forum of a course, where its participants can read it and may be notified by the site. A published announcement cannot be withdrawn through this tool. Called without 'confirm_token', it changes nothing and returns a summary of the change plus a token valid for 5 minutes; called again with the same arguments and that token, it applies the change. Where approval is required it returns 'approval_pending' with a link to a page on the site where the signed-in user approves or rejects the change. Repeating a confirmed call returns the stored result, while a new call without 'idempotency_key' is a new, separate change.

message.description: Text of the announcement, as plain text.

confirm_token.description: Token returned by the first call, sent back with the same arguments to apply the change.

idempotency_key.description: Optional key chosen by the caller. Repeating a call with the same key and arguments returns the stored result instead of requesting the change again.

tools.name: send_message_to_participants
tools.title: Send message to participants
tools.description: Sends one plain text message, through the messaging of the site, to up to 50 named participants of one course. A sent message cannot be withdrawn, and each connection can reach a limited number of recipients per day. Called without 'confirm_token', it changes nothing and returns a summary of the change plus a token valid for 5 minutes; called again with the same arguments and that token, it applies the change. Where approval is required it returns 'approval_pending' with a link to a page on the site where the signed-in user approves or rejects the change. Repeating a confirmed call returns the stored result, while a new call without 'idempotency_key' is a new, separate change.

message.description: Text of the message, as plain text.

confirm_token.description: Token returned by the first call, sent back with the same arguments to apply the change.

idempotency_key.description: Optional key chosen by the caller. Repeating a call with the same key and arguments returns the stored result instead of requesting the change again.

tools.name: set_activity_visibility
tools.title: Set activity visibility
tools.description: Shows or hides one activity or resource of a course for its students, replacing its current visibility. Use it when a teacher asks to hide or show a named activity found with the course outline. Called without 'confirm_token', it changes nothing and returns a summary of the change plus a token valid for 5 minutes; called again with the same arguments and that token, it applies the change. Where approval is required it returns 'approval_pending' with a link to a page on the site where the signed-in user approves or rejects the change. Repeating a confirmed call returns the stored result and does not apply the change twice.

activity_id.description: Identifier of the activity, as returned by 'get_course_outline'.

visible.description: True to show the activity, false to hide it.

confirm_token.description: Token returned by the first call, sent back with the same arguments to apply the change.

idempotency_key.description: Optional key chosen by the caller. Repeating a call with the same key and arguments returns the stored result instead of requesting the change again.

tools.name: update_assignment_dates
tools.title: Update assignment dates
tools.description: Changes one or more of the dates of one assignment: when submissions open, when they are due and the cut-off after which none are accepted, replacing the current values for every student. Dates that are not given stay as they are, and a date cannot be removed through this tool. Called without 'confirm_token', it changes nothing and returns a summary of the change plus a token valid for 5 minutes; called again with the same arguments and that token, it applies the change. Where approval is required it returns 'approval_pending' with a link to a page on the site where the signed-in user approves or rejects the change. Repeating a confirmed call returns the stored result and does not apply the change twice.

assignment_id.description: Identifier of the assignment activity, as returned by 'get_course_outline'.

open_date.description: New opening date as an ISO 8601 date-time with a time zone. Omit it to leave the date as it is.

due_date.description: New due date as an ISO 8601 date-time with a time zone. Omit it to leave the date as it is.

cutoff_date.description: New cut-off date as an ISO 8601 date-time with a time zone. Omit it to leave the date as it is.

confirm_token.description: Token returned by the first call, sent back with the same arguments to apply the change.

idempotency_key.description: Optional key chosen by the caller. Repeating a call with the same key and arguments returns the stored result instead of requesting the change again.

tools.name: enrol_users_in_course
tools.title: Enrol users in course
tools.description: Enrols up to 50 named users in one course with the manual enrolment method and one role, which is the student role unless another is given. Users already enrolled manually keep their enrolment and gain the role; a user whose manual enrolment is suspended or limited in time is refused, because enrolling again would reactivate it. Called without 'confirm_token', it changes nothing and returns a summary of the change plus a token valid for 5 minutes; called again with the same arguments and that token, it applies the change. Where approval is required it returns 'approval_pending' with a link to a page on the site where the signed-in user approves or rejects the change. Repeating a confirmed call returns the stored result and does not apply the change twice.

user_ids.description: Users to enrol, as returned by 'find_users'.

role.description: Short name of the role to give, for example student or teacher.

confirm_token.description: Token returned by the first call, sent back with the same arguments to apply the change.

idempotency_key.description: Optional key chosen by the caller. Repeating a call with the same key and arguments returns the stored result instead of requesting the change again.

tools.name: set_enrolment_status
tools.title: Set enrolment status
tools.description: Requests that the manual enrolment of up to 50 named users in one course be suspended or made active again. A suspended user cannot enter the course, and their enrolment, roles, groups, grades and submissions are all kept, so the change can be undone at any time. Enrolments created by other methods (self, cohort, payment) are not affected, and nobody is unenrolled. It changes nothing by itself: it creates a pending action and returns a link to a page on the site where the signed-in user reviews the change and approves or rejects it. The tool 'get_pending_action_status' returns the outcome.

user_ids.description: Users whose enrolment changes, as returned by 'list_course_participants'.

status.description: 'suspended' to take the access to the course away, 'active' to give it back.

idempotency_key.description: Optional key chosen by the caller. Repeating a call with the same key and arguments returns the stored result instead of requesting the change again.

tools.name: create_course
tools.title: Create course
tools.description: Creates one empty course, with the default settings of the site, in a course category the user manages. The course is always created hidden from students; making it visible is done on the site. Called without 'confirm_token', it changes nothing and returns a summary of the change plus a token valid for 5 minutes; called again with the same arguments and that token, it applies the change. Where approval is required it returns 'approval_pending' with a link to a page on the site where the signed-in user approves or rejects the change. Repeating a confirmed call returns the stored result, while a new call without 'idempotency_key' is a new, separate change.

category_id.description: Category to create the course in, as returned by 'list_categories'.

short_name.description: Short name. It must not be in use by another course.

confirm_token.description: Token returned by the first call, sent back with the same arguments to apply the change.

idempotency_key.description: Optional key chosen by the caller. Repeating a call with the same key and arguments returns the stored result instead of requesting the change again.

tools.name: set_user_suspension
tools.title: Set user suspension
tools.description: Requests the suspension or the reactivation of one user account of the site. A suspended user cannot sign in and is signed out; site administrators and the own account cannot be suspended. It changes nothing by itself: it creates a pending action and returns a link to a page on the site where the signed-in user reviews the change and approves or rejects it. The tool 'get_pending_action_status' returns the outcome.

user_id.description: Account to change, as returned by 'find_users'.

suspended.description: True to suspend the account, false to reactivate it.

idempotency_key.description: Optional key chosen by the caller. Repeating a call with the same key and arguments returns the stored result instead of requesting the change again.

tools.name: post_forum_discussion
tools.title: Post forum discussion
tools.description: Starts one discussion, with a subject and a plain text message and without attachments, in a forum of a course, published as the signed-in user; announcements go through post_course_announcement, and in a forum with groups the group is needed unless the user may post to all of them. Subscribers are e-mailed and a published post cannot be withdrawn through this tool. Called without 'confirm_token', it changes nothing and returns a summary of the change plus a token valid for 5 minutes; called again with the same arguments and that token, it applies the change. Where approval is required it returns 'approval_pending' with a link to a page on the site where the signed-in user approves or rejects the change. Repeating a confirmed call returns the stored result, while a new call without 'idempotency_key' is a new, separate change.

forum_id.description: Course module identifier of the forum, from list_course_forums.

message.description: Text of the post, as plain text.

group_id.description: Group the discussion is for, in a forum that uses groups.

confirm_token.description: Token returned by the first call, sent back with the same arguments to apply the change.

idempotency_key.description: Optional key chosen by the caller. Repeating a call with the same key and arguments returns the stored result instead of requesting the change again.

tools.name: reply_to_forum_post
tools.title: Reply to forum post
tools.description: Publishes one plain text reply to a post of a forum discussion as the signed-in user, never private and never with attachments, and the forum decides whether it is allowed (locked discussions, cut-off dates, groups); it does not edit or delete any post. Subscribers are e-mailed and a published reply cannot be withdrawn through this tool. Called without 'confirm_token', it changes nothing and returns a summary of the change plus a token valid for 5 minutes; called again with the same arguments and that token, it applies the change. Where approval is required it returns 'approval_pending' with a link to a page on the site where the signed-in user approves or rejects the change. Repeating a confirmed call returns the stored result, while a new call without 'idempotency_key' is a new, separate change.

post_id.description: Identifier of the post to answer, from get_forum_discussion.

message.description: Text of the reply, as plain text.

subject.description: Subject line. By default, the subject of the post answered with the usual prefix.

confirm_token.description: Token returned by the first call, sent back with the same arguments to apply the change.

idempotency_key.description: Optional key chosen by the caller. Repeating a call with the same key and arguments returns the stored result instead of requesting the change again.
